text:
Mackenzie Blackwood's first shutout of the season, a 4-0 win over Detroit on Saturday, was a nice reminder of what the Avalanche look like when the goalie isn't a question. They are 10-6-2, have scored four goals a game, and have a 96 percent chance at the playoffs in our simulations.

The scoring has run hot, though. Colorado has 10 more goals than its chances predict, while giving up about five more than its goalies should. Those two gaps tend to close, and the second one matters more for a team that takes 53 percent of the five-on-five expected goals, good but not dominant. Artturi Lehkonen, with 12 goals and a point streak, has been the headline next to Nathan MacKinnon and Martin Necas, a line that has outscored teams 19-9.

The worry is on the blue line. Josh Manson is out up to eight weeks, Mile High Hockey reported, which breaks up the second pair and pushes Noah Juulsen into a real role behind Cale Makar and Devon Toews. Beat writers keep mentioning slow starts too, Saturday included. This is a contender that has been winning on finishing; the next month tells us whether the defense holds without Manson.
headline: Colorado keeps scoring, and Blackwood finally got his shutout
